events.description: AI in Chemical Engineering: teams solve industry-data problems at Easy, Medium and Hard levels using AI/ML.
rules: Open to all years. Team size: 3–4 members.
No cross-year teams.
One Chemical Engineering member is compulsory in every team.
Round 1 – Data Brief: teams choose a difficulty level and submit a one-page abstract of their AI/ML approach.
Round 2 – Mid-Eval Checkpoint: data cleaning, model choice and early results are reviewed.
Round 3 – Final Eval & Pitch: final evaluation of the solution followed by a final deck presentation (maximum 10 slides).

events.description: Consulting event with puzzles, guesstimates and root cause analysis, followed by a business case study presented as a PPT.
rules: Open to all courses and all years.
Team size: 3 members for 1st and 2nd year; 2 members for 3rd year. One Chemical Engineering member is compulsory.
No cross-year teams.
Round 1 – Hustle Bustle: written assessment with puzzles, guesstimates, root cause analysis and reasoning questions in a fixed time.
Round 2 – 80/20: a business case study is released to qualified teams; teams analyse it, resolve ambiguities and present a PPT.

events.description: Teams pitch how they would sell a product and then run a social media campaign judged on reach and engagement.
rules: Team size: 2–4 members. No cross-year teams; one team must be from one year.
One Chemical Engineering member is compulsory in every team.
Round 1 – One-Page Pitch: a one-page deck on how the team would sell the given product.
Round 2 – Impression Wars: shortlisted teams run a social media campaign; ranking is based on impressions and engagement.
Round 3 – Final Pitch: a final deck presentation covering strategy, campaign results and learnings (maximum 10 slides).

events.description: Process simulation challenge: teams model a given problem statement in DWSIM (1st year) or Aspen Plus (2nd and 3rd year).
rules: Team size: 3 members for 1st year; 2 members for 2nd and 3rd year. No cross-year teams; one team must be from one year.
At least one Chemical Engineering member must be in every team.
Software: DWSIM for 1st year; Aspen Plus for 2nd and 3rd year.
Round 1 – Blueprint: each team receives a problem statement and submits a one-page abstract covering assumptions, property package and flowsheet plan.
Round 2 – Mid-Sim Check: mid evaluation of every team's model progress.
Round 3 – Final Run: final evaluation of the converged simulation followed by a final deck presentation.

events.description: Project showcase on emerging and traditional chemical engineering topics, built from a common problem statement.
rules: Open to all years. Team size: 3–4 members. No cross-year teams; one team must be from one year.
At least one Chemical Engineering member must be in every team.
Round 1 – Topic Lock: teams choose a topic from the common problem statement and submit a one-page abstract.
Round 2 – Mid-Expo Review: mid evaluation of project progress.
Round 3 – Final Evaluation: evaluation of the completed project, report or model.
Round 4 – Professors' Panel: final deck presentation before the professors.

events.description: Process safety event: identify missing equipment on a PFD and carry out a HAZOP study on a given problem statement.
rules: Participate solo or in a team of 1–3 members. One Chemical Engineering member is compulsory; the remaining members may be from any branch.
No cross-year teams; one team must be from one year.
Round 1 – Missing Link: fill in the missing equipment on the PFD (quiz for 1st and 2nd year).
Round 2 – Hazard Hunt: teams carry out a HAZOP study and submit a one-page abstract of their approach plus the HAZOP worksheet.
Round 3 – Safety Verdict: final deck presentation of findings, risks and recommended safeguards (maximum 10 slides).

events.description: Mandatory multi-stage assessment for Chemical Engineering students across the core, consultancy and software domains.
rules: Mandatory for all 1st, 2nd and 3rd year Chemical Engineering students.
Individual participation only.
Round 1 – Online Assessment: online test for the core, consultancy and software domains.
Round 2 – Group Discussion: group discussion of all participants.
Round 3 – Interview: interviews of all participants in their respective domains.

events.description: Clue-driven campus hunt where teams solve chemical-engineering-themed clues to find checkpoints.
rules: Mandatory common event. Team size: 3–4 members. No cross-year teams; one team must be from one year.
At least one Chemical Engineering member must be in every team.
Round 1 – Clue Trail: teams solve clues to find checkpoints and collect stamps.
Round 2 – Final Hunt: fastest correct completion wins; finalists submit a three-slide debrief deck of their route and answers.
